text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Right-wing Disy reaches a compromise in Limassol for its candidate in December's municipal elections.
- Police are on the trail a gang of criminals in Limassol connected to robberies and burglaries.
- Limassol and Paphos were rocked by a quake measuring 4.9 on the Richter scale yesterday.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Schoolchildren are urged to show restraint at protests against the 13th anniversary from the creation of the illegal regime (in north Cyprus)
- Ex-drug squad boss claims to have a tape recording of a drug dealer claiming to have been tipped off by a member of his team.
- La Ciccolina talks about life, the universe and the Cyprus problem.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Cyprus Airways is expected to break even in the second half of 1996.
- Era Split Capital is to proceed with a 6 million IPO.
- Cyprus trade deficit goes up to 716 million.
HARAVGHI
- Municipal elections cause friction within Disy party.
- Co-operatives and small shopkeepers disagree with abolishing ceiling on interest rates.
- Woman attacks her pregnant social worker, sending her to hospital.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- American diplomats focus on defusing military tension in Cyprus.
- The government is to increase penalties for tax dodgers.
SIMERINI
- Disy faces tough hours after disagreements expressed within the party over candidates to run in municipal elections.
